packageRules.description: Group all non-major updates by manager — keeps majors as individual PRs for review. Specific rules below (vite, go version, terraform) override per Renovate's last-rule-wins semantics.

Gate major version bumps behind the Dependency Dashboard for human review (audit finding I-7). automerge is already false by default; requiring approval prevents automatic branch creation and CI runs.
Pin PostGIS to PostgreSQL v17 - major version bumps require database migration
Keep every Go patch pin in one PR: Dockerfiles, go.mod directives, and the custom managers for go.work and CI's GO_VERSION. The gomod bump rule below opts the minimum-version directives into updates.
Update the go.mod Go directives with the toolchain pins. Renovate otherwise treats them as compatibility floors and leaves them unchanged.
Allow Go 1.26 Docker patch tags with compatibility suffixes. The semver range 1.26.x treats -alpine as a prerelease and rejects it; Docker preserves the existing suffix separately.
Track x/net security fixes even when it is indirect. The default gomod manager disables indirect updates; waiting for a parent module to upgrade can leave a reachable HTTP/2 vulnerability pinned.
Pin @vitejs/plugin-react to v5 until Babel → @rolldown/plugin-babel migration
Group Vite ecosystem so peer-dep-coupled major bumps land in one PR
Group all Terraform updates into one PR

Keep every uv pin in one PR. The Dockerfile tag and pyproject.toml's [tool.uv] required-version must move together — uv.lock carries a format revision, so a uv newer than the image's can write a lock the production build can't read. Must stay after the group-by-manager rule above to win under last-rule-wins.

Hold CPython at 3.14.x: pants `interpreter_constraints` (>=3.14,<3.15) and pyproject `requires-python` forbid 3.15. packages/stravapipe/.python-version (pyenv manager) is the only patch pin; the stravapipe Dockerfile and CI's integration job both install from it with the pinned uv, so a patch that uv has no download for fails that PR's CI. Must stay after the group-by-manager rule to win under last-rule-wins.

Keep every Flyway pin in one PR. The schemas/database/Dockerfile tag and the `docker run` tag in ci.yml's migration step must move together, and both must stay in step with the deploy repo's flyway-migrate action — a migration verified in CI by one Flyway version but applied to prod by another is the drift the pin exists to prevent. Must stay after the group-by-manager rule to win under last-rule-wins.

customManagers.description: Track the CI Go patch pin. The github-actions manager cannot resolve setup-go's go-version from env.GO_VERSION.
Track the workspace Go patch pin. The gomod manager extracts go.mod files, not go.work; use the same dependency name to join the go version group.
Track [tool.uv] required-version as the uv image, so it bumps alongside the Dockerfile tag rather than drifting silently.

Track the Flyway image the CI migration step runs via `docker run flyway/flyway:X` — a raw shell command the github-actions manager does not parse, so without this the tag would silently rot at whatever was pinned. The schemas/database/Dockerfile FROM is covered by the dockerfile manager; the `flyway` packageRule above keeps both in one PR.
